proposal: The Mandate recommends that HUD repeal the AFFH regulation that the Biden Administration reinstated, along with other uses of special-purpose credit authorities to advance equity. It treats this as a first-year administrative action and notes in a footnote that the Biden Administration had proposed a replacement for the 2020 Trump-era rule.

status_summary: HUD announced on 2025-02-27 that it was terminating the AFFH rule and published an interim final rule on 2025-03-03 (90 FR 11020, effective 2025-04-02) that repeals the 2021 interim final rule and the 1994 Analysis of Impediments requirements. Under the interim rule, a grantee's certification is met if it took any action rationally related to promoting fair housing, and no specific planning process is required. The comment period closed 2025-05-09, and a Federal Register search of HUD documents through 2026-10-01 showed no final rule, so the interim rule remains the operative text. No court challenge to the interim rule was found; 19 state attorneys general filed a comment letter opposing it. The Mandate's companion call to end other equity-related uses of special-purpose credit authorities has also been acted on: HUD withdrew its special purpose credit guidance (2026-04-06 and 2026-07-17), the CFPB amended Regulation B's special purpose credit provisions (2026-04-22) and rescinded a 2020 advisory opinion on for-profit programs (2026-06-17), and eight agencies including HUD jointly rescinded the 2022 Interagency Statement (2026-08-25).

timeline.event: HUD Secretary Scott Turner announces HUD is terminating the AFFH rule (HUD press release No. 25-034; date taken from a trade-group report published 2025-02-28).
HUD publishes the interim final rule 'Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Revisions' (90 FR 11020; effective 2025-04-02; comments due 2025-05-02), repealing the 2021 interim final rule.
A coalition of 19 state attorneys general, led by California, Massachusetts and New York, files a comment letter urging HUD to withdraw the interim rule (a comment letter, not a lawsuit).
HUD extends the comment deadline on the interim rule to 2025-05-09 after a Regulations.gov technical problem.
Related action: HUD proposes to rescind its Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing regulations (24 CFR part 108 and part of part 200), a separate rule from AFFH (90 FR 23491; comments closed 2025-07-03).

HUD publishes a notice (91 FR 17291) withdrawing eight Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity guidance documents, including the FHEO Statement on the Fair Housing Act and Special Purpose Credit Programs dated 2021-12-07; the notice gives an effective date of 2025-09-17 for the withdrawal.
CFPB publishes a final rule amending Regulation B, including its special purpose credit program provisions.
CFPB publishes a rule rescinding its December 2020 advisory opinion on certain special purpose credit programs run by for-profit organizations.

HUD publishes a notice (91 FR 44867) withdrawing thirteen Office of General Counsel guidance documents, including the 2021-12-06 guidance on the Fair Housing Act's treatment of certain special purpose credit programs; the notice gives an effective date of 2025-09-25.
Eight federal agencies including HUD, DOJ, CFPB and Treasury rescind the 2022 Interagency Statement on Special Purpose Credit Programs.

title: Repeal the Biden-era Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing (AFFH) rule
uncertainties: A 2026 litigation search returned only 2018-era suits over the earlier rule suspension and the 2025 attorneys general comment letter, so no suit against the 2025 interim rule was found, but the search was one query. The Federal Register listing reviewed shows the first 20 of 33 matching HUD documents. The special purpose credit documents were identified from titles and abstracts and were not read in full, and their scope relative to the Mandate's wording was not compared. The HUD press release page loaded without body text, so the 2025-02-27 date comes from a trade-group article. On 2026-10-30 a Federal Register query for HUD fair housing documents from 2026-09-25 and two web searches (final rule, litigation) found no AFFH final rule and no suit; web results were limited to older rule history and are negative search results, not events.
